tools.description: Return a fast, zero-argument health overview of the running Cruma agent. Reports an overall status (ok / degraded / critical) and a structured list of active issues across: hosted-process health (crashes, backoff, start failures), listener binding failures, config validation errors, certificate expiry or ACME failures, tunnel connectivity, and HTTP error rates from the last 10 minutes. Use this as the first call when troubleshooting — it bootstraps context before diving into specific tools.
tools.name: get_health_summary

tools.description: Make a local port reachable through this agent's tunnel. Omit access for a public share, or set its closed password, ip_allowlist, or sign_in access policy. Creates (or updates, if the name or port is already exposed) a backend for host:port (default 127.0.0.1) and a tunnel-only frontend at <name>.<assigned domain>, waits up to 30 s for the tunnel to have its public domain, and returns public_url, local_target, frontend_id and account. The share lasts until unexpose or until the agent stops (over the local socket: until that socket connection closes): no config save writes it to the config file, including later persist=true calls. Withdraw it with unexpose.

password.description:
Password for HTTP Basic authentication. A strong password is
generated when omitted and returned once in the exposure result.

cidrs.description: CIDR networks allowed to reach the share.

anyOf.description:
Cruma-account sign-in. It is typed now so callers can handle the
unavailable-provider result without guessing at OAuth settings.

Closed, temporary access policies for an MCP share. These are translated
into frontend-only middleware and never become persistent configuration.

access.description: Optional temporary access policy. Omit it to leave the share public.

host.description: Local host or IP the server listens on. Default: `127.0.0.1`.

name.description:
Subdomain label for the public hostname (`<name>.<assigned domain>`):
lowercase letters, digits and `-`, at most 63 characters. Default: the
name this port is already exposed under, otherwise `port-<port>`.

port.description: Local TCP port the server listens on (1-65535).

tools.name: expose_local_port

tools.description: List every live temporary port and directory share created through expose_local_port or expose_local_directory, including its kind, name, local target, public URL, and safe access-policy details, plus the tunnel's account. Passwords are never returned. Shares are never written to the config file.

kind.description: Restrict the result to port or directory shares. Default: all shares.

tools.name: list_shares

tools.description: Stop serving a temporary port or directory share created by expose_local_port or expose_local_directory: removes exactly the backend and frontend that call created, so its public URL no longer reaches the local target. Pass the returned name (or frontend_id). Fails for names those tools did not create.

name.description: The `name` (equal to the `frontend_id`) returned by either expose tool.

tools.name: unexpose
list_agents
tools.description: List the Cruma agents running for this user (the desktop app, headless agents, and this session's own agent) and the profiles that are not running. Each running agent shows its `version` and release `channel` (stable and preview agents can run side by side), when it started (`started_at`, `age_secs`) and who started it (`starter`: user_start, installed_service, desktop_app or coding_session with the client and process id when known, unknown for an agent that does not record it), plus its tunnel domain, whether the tunnel is anonymous or signed-in account state, its server-reported tunnel plan when known, its sites (hostnames) and hosted processes, whether changes made here are saved, and whether it also serves HTTP /mcp. The build, start and starter facts show even when an agent does not answer in time; the live facts then are absent. `attached` marks the agent every other tool here talks to. A profile that is not running comes with a `start_hint`; this tool never starts one.
